key_insight: In Alzheimer’s disease research, strong AI segmentation accuracy did not guarantee preservation of biologically meaningful associations between perivascular spaces and amyloid biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: AI-derived perivascular space measurements require cohort-specific validation before they can reliably support Alzheimer’s disease biomarker research.
method: Benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based segmentation models against manual MRI labels.
Evaluated segmentation across brain regions, diagnoses, scanners, and lesion burdens.
Tested whether model-derived measurements reproduced manual-label associations with Alzheimer’s-related biomarkers.
evidence_signal: Across 60 ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans, ADNI-PVS-Net achieved internal Dice of 0.58 ± 0.14 but external Dice ≤0.11; only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS–amyloid relationship.
watch_item: Some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as perivascular spaces, potentially distorting downstream biological inference.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
